sentence: This project studies how a fusion protein and a helper protein reshape chromatin to drive a leukemia of young children.
This project studies how individual neurons build and keep a daily rhythm in the body, and how disrupting it leads to disease.
This project designs and tests a mobile health system with wearable sensors that gives real-time help to young adults with depression and anxiety.
This project runs shared animal studies, laboratory services and aerosol infection work for research on dangerous infectious disease germs under high containment.
This project studies how a mutated gene called calreticulin causes a group of blood disorders in which the body makes too many blood cells.
This project tries to find out how adults with lupus experience brain fog, and how it changes from day to day.
This project provides sequencing, culture and germ-free mouse services so researchers can study how gut microbes affect digestive diseases.
This project builds a long-term 3D mouse liver model to study how pregnancy changes liver cells and drug-processing enzymes.
This project builds an AI tool that finds and locates abnormal brain electrical spikes in EEG recordings, using the physics of the brain.
This project tries to find out how the time of day of cancer treatment changes brain inflammation and thinking problems.
This project studies how a double-stranded RNA element and upstream open reading frames control protein production in heart muscle cells.
This project studies how a person's stress reactivity relates to differences between Black and White women in pregnancy and placenta problems.
This project builds electronic clothing for the leg that measures pressure between the body and a prosthesis or orthosis outside the laboratory.
This project studies how human genes have evolved over time to fight viruses and other germs, to find how the body resists infection.
This project manages shared laboratory cores that give cancer researchers access to specialized equipment and expert services.
This project studies how a gene called PYDC5 protects against colorectal cancer, and tries to find the molecular steps involved.
This project builds deep learning tools that combine genetics with single-cell data to understand the causes of complex human diseases.
This project builds computer programs that use credit records to spot people who may be at risk of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
This project develops a way to combine capillary electrophoresis with native mass spectrometry to identify changes that cause charge variants in protein medicines.
